title: The Return of the Walking Dead - Revisiting Here's Negan: The Board Game
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fj2SC2FA324

Daniel (@dungeondive) calls **The Walking Dead: Here's Negan** highly underrated — underrated enough that he forgot to put it on his own top 50, which he now regards as a mistake. Mantic's pitch, as he frames it: the tension of Space Hulk, but fully co-op, and therefore genuinely good solo in a way Space Hulk's variants never manage.

The structure is escort-plus-secure. Negan walks a predetermined dotted route across the map and the survivors must get him to the far end alive. He will not open a door, because he expects doors opened for him, and he will not enter an unsecured room — and if forced to, he enrages, swings the bat, strips reputation and stamina from anyone nearby and pulls more walkers in. His behaviour comes off a small AI deck that Daniel describes as the thing you will learn to love and hate; he has never hated a plastic figure more.

Walkers enter as face-down tokens resolved only on line of sight, lifted straight from Space Hulk, and Daniel wants more games doing it. Survivors hold a competing reputation track under the co-op, and a critical hit means a bite, which makes zero stamina fatal.

His verdict: worth sixty dollars, a must-buy near forty. The tiles look dull; everything else is high quality.

----

Negan is an ally who sabotages you constantly. Which game NPC did you most enjoy being stuck with?
